ESB.tagline: The beating heart of modern Turkey
ESB.intro: Ankara is a sophisticated capital city that perfectly blends ancient history with a vibrant, student-friendly energy. It offers a unique window into Turkish identity, away from the tourist crowds of the coast.
ESB.didYouKnow: Ankara is famous for its unique cat breed, the Ankara Cat, which is known for its silky white fur and heterochromatic eyes.

highlights.title: Anıtkabir
highlights.note: The monumental mausoleum of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk.

highlights.title: Ankara Castle
highlights.note: Historic citadel offering panoramic city views.

highlights.title: Museum of Anatolian Civilizations
highlights.note: World-class collection of prehistoric artifacts.

highlights.title: Kızılay Square
highlights.note: The buzzing central hub of city nightlife.

food.intro: Ankara’s food scene is defined by hearty Central Anatolian classics and budget-friendly street eats perfect for students.

dishes.name: Ankara Tava
dishes.note: A rich, slow-cooked lamb and orzo pasta dish.

dishes.name: Döner

dishes.name: Bazlama
dishes.note: A soft, fluffy traditional circular flatbread.

dishes.name: Simit
dishes.note: Crispy, molasses-dipped sesame encrusted bread rings.

history.overview: Ankara has been a vital crossroads for civilizations including the Hittites, Romans, and Seljuks. Its historical significance surged in 1923 when it was declared the capital of the newly founded Republic of Turkey. Today, it stands as a testament to the nation's journey from an empire to a modern secular state.

periods.description: Settled by the Hittites and later transformed into a prosperous trading hub under the Romans. The ruins of the Temple of Augustus still stand as proof of this era.
The city became an important strategic outpost for Byzantine and Seljuk rulers. Its castle walls were repeatedly reinforced to withstand frequent regional invasions.
Following WWI, Atatürk established Ankara as the capital to symbolize a clean break from the Ottoman past. It was rapidly transformed from a small town into a sprawling metropolis.

figures.name: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk
figures.role: Founder and first president of modern Turkey

figures.name: Tamerlane
figures.role: Central Asian conqueror who defeated Bayezid I

tips.title: Transportation
tips.note: Use the AnkaraKart for seamless travel on the metro and buses.

tips.title: Walking Tours
tips.note: Explore the historic Ulus district on foot to find hidden artisan workshops.

tips.title: Nightlife
tips.note: Head to Tunalı Hilmi Street for trendy cafes and student hangouts.

AYT.tagline: Where ancient history meets Mediterranean sunshine
AYT.intro: Antalya is the ultimate student escape, blending crystal-clear turquoise waters with a labyrinthine Old Town. It serves as the perfect base to explore majestic Roman ruins and vibrant nightlife without breaking the bank.
AYT.didYouKnow: The city is home to the world's best-preserved Roman theater, Aspendos, which still hosts live opera performances today.

highlights.title: Kaleiçi
highlights.note: Historic Old Town with Ottoman-era houses and boutique cafes.

highlights.title: Hadrian's Gate
highlights.note: An ornate Roman triumphal arch marking the city entrance.

highlights.title: Düden Waterfalls
highlights.note: Dramatic waterfalls cascading directly into the Mediterranean Sea.

highlights.title: Konyaaltı Beach
highlights.note: A massive pebble beach perfect for swimming and sunbathing.

food.intro: Antalya offers a delicious mix of fresh Mediterranean produce and traditional Turkish flavors. Street food here is affordable, filling, and perfect for students on the move.

dishes.name: Piyaz
dishes.note: Bean salad with tahini, a local Antalya specialty.

dishes.name: Gözleme
dishes.note: Thin dough stuffed with spinach, cheese, or spiced meat.

dishes.name: Şiş Köfte
dishes.note: Succulent grilled meatballs served on skewers with fresh pita.

dishes.name: Kabak Tatlısı
dishes.note: Sweet pumpkin dessert served with tahini and walnuts.

history.overview: Founded in the 2nd century BC by the King of Pergamon, Attalus II, the city has long been a vital Mediterranean port. Throughout the centuries, it transitioned through Roman, Byzantine, and Seljuk rule, leaving behind a rich archaeological footprint. Today, it stands as a major hub where modern tourism preserves the echoes of ancient civilizations.

periods.description: Founded as Attaleia, it served as a key naval base for the kingdom of Pergamon. It later flourished under Roman rule, becoming a primary gateway to the East.
The city was conquered by the Seljuk Turks in the early 13th century. This era introduced iconic Islamic architecture that defines the city's skyline today.
Following the collapse of the Ottoman Empire, Antalya transformed into Turkey’s tourism capital. Massive urban development has since turned the city into a global Mediterranean hub.

figures.name: Attalus II
figures.role: King of Pergamon and founder of Antalya

figures.name: Hadrian
figures.role: Roman Emperor who visited the city in 130 AD

tips.title: Use public transport
tips.note: The Antray tram system is cheap and connects major sites.

tips.title: Haggle respectfully
tips.note: In local bazaars, gentle bargaining is expected and quite normal.

HER.tagline: Where ancient myths meet vibrant city life
HER.intro: Heraklion is the pulsating heart of Crete, offering an unparalleled mix of Bronze Age history and modern Mediterranean energy. It is the perfect base for students looking to balance legendary archaeological exploration with a legendary nightlife scene.
HER.didYouKnow: The Palace of Knossos was once considered a mythical labyrinth, but was proven to be the center of the advanced Minoan civilization.

highlights.title: Palace of Knossos
highlights.note: The massive, colorful seat of Minoan power.

highlights.title: Heraklion Archaeological Museum
highlights.note: World's most comprehensive collection of Minoan artifacts.

highlights.title: Koules Fortress
highlights.note: A striking Venetian harbor fortification from the 1500s.

highlights.title: Morosini Fountain
highlights.note: A historic Venetian-era social hub in Lion Square.

food.intro: Crete offers a distinct culinary identity characterized by fresh mountain herbs, local olive oil, and artisanal cheeses.

dishes.name: Dakos
dishes.note: Rusks topped with chopped tomatoes, feta, and olive oil.

dishes.name: Kalitsounia
dishes.note: Small pastries filled with mizithra cheese or wild greens.

dishes.name: Chochlioi Bourbouristoi
dishes.note: Fried snails cooked with rosemary and red wine vinegar.

dishes.name: Gamopilafo
dishes.note: Traditional wedding rice cooked in rich goat meat broth.

history.overview: Heraklion has been a vital Mediterranean crossroads for millennia, serving as a maritime hub for various empires. From its origins as the port of Knossos to its intense Venetian and Ottoman periods, the city is a layered testament to conquest and cultural exchange.

periods.description: This era defined the island as the home of Europe's oldest advanced civilization. The massive palace complex at Knossos dominated the surrounding landscape during this time.
The Venetians turned Heraklion into a formidable fortress known as 'Candia.' They constructed the massive city walls that still define the historic old town today.
Following unification with Greece in the early 20th century, Heraklion grew into a vibrant capital. It remains the educational and economic powerhouse of the island.

figures.name: Nikos Kazantzakis
figures.role: World-renowned author of Zorba the Greek

figures.name: King Minos
figures.role: Legendary mythical ruler of the Minoans

tips.title: Avoid Midday Heat
tips.note: Schedule archaeological site visits early in the morning to beat the intense Mediterranean sun.

tips.title: Student Discounts
tips.note: Always carry your international student ID card to receive significantly reduced museum entry fees.

tips.title: Bus Travel
tips.note: Use the KTEL bus station near the port to travel affordably between Crete's major cities.

tips.title: Hydration
tips.note: Carry a refillable water bottle, as the public fountains throughout the city provide high-quality drinking water.

BOJ.tagline: Where the Black Sea meets urban energy.
BOJ.intro: Burgas is a vibrant coastal hub that perfectly balances industrial history with a laid-back, sun-drenched student vibe. It serves as the gateway to the southern Black Sea coast, offering sprawling sea parks, sandy beaches, and a thriving nightlife scene.
BOJ.didYouKnow: The iconic Sea Garden of Burgas features a famous 'Bridge' that stretches 300 meters into the Black Sea, serving as the city’s favorite meeting spot.

highlights.title: The Sea Garden
highlights.note: A massive, lush waterfront park perfect for chilling.

highlights.title: Burgas Bridge
highlights.note: An iconic pier extending into the Black Sea.

highlights.title: St. Anastasia Island
highlights.note: A mysterious island accessible by boat with rich history.

highlights.title: Atanasovsko Lake
highlights.note: Famous for its natural healing pink mud baths.

dishes.name: Tarator

history.overview: Burgas evolved from a small fishing village into a major maritime and industrial center. Its strategic location on the coast has made it a historical crossroads for various civilizations throughout the centuries. Today, it stands as a modern cultural heart of the Bulgarian seaside.

periods.description: The region was populated by Thracian tribes and later established as a trading post by ancient Greeks. It served as a vital maritime hub connecting inland settlements to the sea.
Known as Pyrgos, it functioned as a small but significant port for trade during the Ottoman rule. It slowly grew in importance due to its sheltered bay and shipping capabilities.
The city flourished in the late 19th century following the liberation of Bulgaria. It transformed into an essential industrial port and a center for oil refining and transportation.

figures.name: Hristo Fotev

tips.note: Knowing basic alphabet helps with reading signs and bus destinations.

tips.title: Stay hydrated
tips.note: Summer temperatures can spike, so keep a water bottle handy.

PDV.tagline: Europe's oldest living city awaits you
PDV.intro: Plovdiv is a vibrant student-friendly hub where ancient Roman ruins blend seamlessly with a bohemian artistic atmosphere. Its colorful Revival-era architecture and bustling cafe culture make it the perfect destination for history buffs and backpackers alike.
PDV.didYouKnow: Plovdiv is officially the oldest continuously inhabited city in Europe, with roots dating back over 8,000 years.

highlights.title: Ancient Theater of Philippopolis
highlights.note: Perfectly preserved Roman theater still used for live performances.

highlights.title: Kapana Creative District
highlights.note: A trendy maze of artisan shops, cafes, and galleries.

highlights.title: Old Town
highlights.note: Cobbled streets lined with colorful 19th-century Bulgarian Revival houses.

highlights.title: Nebet Tepe
highlights.note: The highest hill offering panoramic sunset views over the city.

food.intro: The local food scene is a delicious mix of Balkan tradition and fresh, Mediterranean-inspired produce. You can find affordable, hearty meals at every corner of the city.

dishes.name: Tarator

history.overview: Plovdiv's history spans millennia, serving as a pivotal crossroads for Thracian, Roman, Byzantine, and Ottoman civilizations. This layering of cultures has left behind an unparalleled architectural legacy. Today, it stands as a testament to European persistence and cultural evolution.

periods.description: The city began as a fortified settlement known as Eumolpias. Thracian tribes built the first structures on the city's seven iconic hills.
Under Roman rule, the city became a major cultural center called Trimontium. They constructed grand stadiums, theaters, and aqueducts that still stand today.
During the 19th century, the city saw an economic boom and architectural revolution. Wealthy merchants built the ornate, colorful mansions found in the Old Town.

figures.name: Philip II of Macedon
figures.role: Macedonian king who conquered and renamed the city.

figures.name: Konstantin Velichkov
figures.role: Prominent Bulgarian writer and public figure.

tips.title: Wear comfy shoes
tips.note: The historic center is paved with uneven cobblestones that are difficult for heels.

tips.title: Free Walking Tours
tips.note: Join the daily free walking tours to understand the city's complex layers.

tips.title: Carry some cash
tips.note: While many places accept cards, smaller cafes and markets prefer Bulgarian Lev.

tips.title: Respect the hills
tips.note: Plovdiv is built on seven hills, so expect plenty of uphill walking.

AMS.tagline: Canals, culture, and endless student energy.
AMS.intro: Amsterdam is a vibrant maze of historic canals and world-class museums that pulses with youthful energy. It perfectly blends a rich artistic legacy with a forward-thinking, laid-back modern lifestyle.
AMS.didYouKnow: Amsterdam is built on millions of wooden poles driven into the soft marshy ground to support its buildings.

highlights.title: Rijksmuseum

history.overview: Amsterdam began as a humble 13th-century fishing village on the Amstel River. It blossomed into a global trading powerhouse during the Golden Age and remains a beacon of tolerance. Today, it stands as a major European hub for education, art, and international commerce.

periods.description: Founded as a small dam on the Amstel in the 1200s. It quickly grew into a bustling port for regional trade.
During the 17th century, Amsterdam became the world's richest trade center. Massive wealth funded the iconic canal rings we see today.
The city transformed into a global center for arts and tourism. It remains an open, liberal society known for innovation.
